summary:
Echoes of Orbit is an interactive educational web museum designed for the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. We developed a lightweight, browser-based platform that tells the stories of NASA’s discarded rovers, landers, and probes left across the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space—including Opportunity, Ingenuity, Apollo 11, Apollo 15, Viking 1, and Cassini.
Instead of static text, Echoes of Orbit combines verified NASA landing coordinates and mission timelines with "Voices of the Void"—immersive, first-person audio narratives generated via speech synthesis that allow each spacecraft to share its final memories with students. By pairing emotional storytelling with interactive celestial filters and a STEM knowledge-check quiz, our project transforms silent space hardware into relatable pioneers, inspiring the next generation of explorers to value humanity's off-world scientific heritage.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
Echoes of Orbit is a zero-install, responsive web application that serves as a virtual museum of space exploration heritage. Users can filter iconic NASA hardware by location (The Moon, Mars, and Deep Space) to inspect each mission's operational timeline, exact landing coordinates, and scientific breakthroughs. Each exhibit features a "Listen to Machine's Voice" button powered by the Web Speech API, reading a custom first-person monologue written from the spacecraft's perspective. At the bottom of the platform, an interactive Knowledge Check quiz tests students' comprehension of the missions they explored.
Benefits & Intended Impact
Designed primarily for K-12 students and space enthusiasts, Echoes of Orbit bridges the gap between raw historical archives and engaging STEM education. By giving a "voice" to silent machines like the Opportunity rover and the Ingenuity helicopter, the project fosters empathy, curiosity, and awareness of space archaeology and planetary protection.
Tools, Coding Languages & Creativity
We built the application using semantic HTML5, modern CSS3 (with custom space-themed radial gradients and responsive grid layouts), and vanilla JavaScript (ES6) leveraging the browser's native Web Speech Synthesis API for accessible audio narration without requiring heavy external audio files.
Transparency & Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure
In compliance with NASA Space Apps guidelines, Large Language Models (LLMs) were used to assist in structuring the HTML/CSS/JS codebase, drafting the first-person educational narratives, and generating promotional cover artwork (clearly labeled as SI-generated). All scientific facts, mission dates, and planetary coordinates were cross-verified against official NASA archives.
